surprises.head: The Rangers had to shorten their bench
surprises.body: After Joseph Veleno left in the first period, the Rangers’ bottom-six forwards played 35% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 42% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: The Rangers got the good looks
surprises.body: The Rangers’ shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% (about 6.3% against Utah) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: The Rangers beat the Mammoth
paras: The Rangers’ Joseph Veleno left in the first period and didn’t return. Vladislav Gavrikov opened the scoring for the Rangers late in the period, but Nick Schmaltz tied it 1-1 for Utah on the power play late in the second. The third period was a wild one. Will Cuylle and Jack McBain fought early in the period, and Gabe Perreault put the Rangers ahead for good early in the period. J.T. Miller made it 3-1 midway through the period, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Andrew Peeke scored his first goal for Utah just over two minutes later to pull the Mammoth within one. Eeli Tolvanen ended any hope of a comeback with an empty-netter with a little over a minute left.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Igor Shesterkin made 28 saves for the Rangers, and Karel Vejmelka stopped 18 of 21. By our Swing measure, Adam Fox had the best night of anyone. The Rangers improved to 3-1-0, and the Mammoth fell to 2-1-0.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Rangers.
Nick Schmaltz has scored in every game this season.
All three of the preview’s calls held.
